about.title: King City Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Defective products don't announce themselves — a lawn tool that shatters, a car part that fails on San Antonio Drive, a space heater that ignites without warning. In King City, a farming and agriculture-rooted community of under 14,000 people, product failures can happen at home, on a ranch, or on the job with heavy equipment. California's strict liability rule matters here: an injured person generally doesn't have to prove the manufacturer was careless, only that the product was defective and that the defect caused harm. That's a real advantage compared to typical negligence cases. We handle product liability claims for King City residents who've been hurt by defective products. Our team can evaluate your claim, identify who in the supply chain may be responsible, and pursue compensation on a contingency basis, meaning there's no fee unless money is recovered.

whyChoose.title: Why King City Residents Choose Us

items.title: Strict Liability Can Simplify Your Case
items.desc: California generally doesn't require proof the manufacturer was negligent — only that the product was defective and caused injury, which can streamline what needs to be shown.

items.title: Multiple Parties May Share Responsibility
items.desc: Manufacturers, distributors, and even retailers who sold the product can potentially be held liable, giving us more avenues to pursue accountability.

items.title: Preserving the Product Matters Early
items.desc: We can advise you on keeping the defective product intact and unaltered, since it often serves as the central piece of evidence in a strict liability claim.

items.question: Do I need to prove the manufacturer was careless?
items.answer: Not necessarily. Under California's strict liability standard for defective products, you generally need to show the product was defective and that the defect caused your injury — not that anyone was negligent. We can help determine which type of defect applies to your situation.

items.question: What should I do with the product that hurt me?
items.answer: Try to keep it exactly as it was after the incident, without repairing, cleaning, or discarding it. The product itself is often the most important evidence in these claims, so preserving it helps our investigation.

items.question: Are product liability claims common in a smaller community like King City?
items.answer: King City's population is under 14,000, so individual defective product cases may not appear in local news the way traffic collisions do. Still, agricultural equipment, household products, and vehicle parts used throughout Monterey County can fail just as they might anywhere else, and residents here have the same legal protections.

items.question: Do you charge anything upfront?
items.answer: No. We handle product liability claims on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless you recover compensation.
